questions.solutionHtml:
NOD 2
  • Crohn's disease is associated with NOD2, which is also known as the CARD15 gene.
  • NOD2 encodes for a protein involved in the innate immune system that recognizes bacterial components and triggers an inflammatory response. (activates signaling events, including the NF-κB pathway)
  • Mutations in the NOD2 gene have been found to be more common in individuals with Crohn's disease compared to the general population


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 621,622

questions.stem: A 35-year-old male presents with blood and mucus in his stools for the past month, along with abdominal pain and cramping. Barium enema shows a lead-pipe appearance. Which of the following is more specifically seen in this condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Pseudopolyposis
  • The given clinical scenario with findings of lead-pipe appearance on Barium enema is suggestive of Ulcerative colitis.
  • Pseudopolyposis is a characteristic feature of Ulcerative colitis, which refers to the formation of multiple polyp-like growths of inflamed mucosa in the colon.
  • These growths are not true polyps, but rather a result of the repeated cycles of inflammation and healing in the mucosa.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 621,622

questions.stem: Which of the following is an extraintestinal manifestation associated with Crohn's disease?
questions.solutionHtml:
All of the above
  • Erythema nodosum, uveitis, and kidney stones are all extraintestinal manifestations of IBD


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 621,622

questions.stem: Which of the following would be the best morphological feature to distinguish ulcerative colitis from Crohn’s disease:
questions.solutionHtml:
Diffuse distributions of pseudopolyps
  • Pseudopolyps are seen only in UC.
  • Isolated islands of regenerating mucosa often bulge into the lumen to create pseudopolyps, and the tips of these polyps may fuse to create mucosal bridges


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 621,622

questions.solutionHtml:
Ulcerative colitis involves mucosa and submucosa

  • Option: C is true: Ulcerative colitis involves only the mucosa and submucosa, not the deeper layers of the intestinal wall.

questions.stem: What is the most common site of regional enterprises?
questions.solutionHtml:
Distal ileum and colon
  • Crohn's disease is also called regional enteritis.
  • It most commonly affects the terminal ileum and cecum, but any site within the gastrointestinal tract can be involved; skip lesions are common and noncaseating granulomas also occur


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 621,622

questions.stem: Which of the following is a specific complication of ulcerative colitis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Toxic megacolon
  • Toxic megacolon is a severe and potentially life-threatening complication of ulcerative colitis.
  • It occurs when the colon becomes dilated and distended due to inflammation, leading to a loss of muscle tone and function.
  • This can result in symptoms such as abdominal distension, severe pain, fever, dehydration, and shock.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 621,622

questions.stem: Which of the following serological markers is positive for Crohn's disease?
questions.solutionHtml:
ASCA
  • ASCA (Anti-Saccharomyces cerevisiae antibodies) is the serological marker that is positive in Crohn's disease.
  • These antibodies are directed against a specific yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) that is commonly found in the gut, and they are present in up to 60% of patients with Crohn's disease.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 621,622

questions.stem: All are seen in Ulcerative colitis except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Skip lesions
  • The presence of multiple, separate, sharply delineated areas of disease, resulting in skip lesions, is characteristic of Crohn's disease and may help in the differentiation from ulcerative colitis.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 621,622

questions.stem: Which of the following conditions is most commonly associated with the development of a fistula?
questions.solutionHtml:
Crohn’s disease
  • Crohn's disease is most commonly associated with the development of a fistula.
  • It is a type of inflammatory bowel disease characterized by transmural inflammation, which can lead to the formation of abnormal connections, or fistulas, between different parts of the gut or between the gut and other organs.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 621,622

questions.stem: A 28-year-old female presents with chronic abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss. She reports having these symptoms for the past 6 months. Yellowish exudates at multiple sites were seen in colonoscopy. What is the likely diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Crohn's disease
  • The given clinical history of chronic abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss, in combination with the finding of yellowish exudates at multiple sites seen in colonoscopy, is suggestive of Crohn's disease.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 621,622
